comparison: Perfect agreement on community composition findings (C34-C35). Both accept the NMDS visualization showing differential effects of GN vs CK treatments on eDNA community structure, with reviewers not challenging these multivariate results.

Strong agreement on eDNA methodology (C56-C58, C103-C106). OpenEval finds the methodological discussion and limitations appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewers accept the quantitative eDNA approach as a methodological contribution, noting it 'provides solutions for the sequencing data.'

Partial agreement on future potential (C61-C62, C101-C102, C109-C117). OpenEval supports the proof-of-concept framing and future directions. Peer reviewers are more cautious, acknowledging novelty but emphasizing 'limited impact due to missing functional validation' and need for 'more data and evidence.'

Agreement on growth and yield findings (C36, C38, C80). Both acknowledge modest cumulative growth effects, lack of daily rate differences, and absence of yield effects. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'did not increase rice yield, but rather rice growth rate' and accept small effects as a limitation.

Significant disagreement on main conclusions (C60, C79, C118). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mixed evidence and overstated effectiveness. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN but more critically, stating results 'did not fully support' the approach and study is 'too preliminary,' needing 'more data and evidence.'

Disagreement on 2019 manipulation validation (C29-C31, C92-C94). OpenEval finds GN effects supported despite acknowledging limitations. Peer reviewers are more critical, stating authors 'did not check the fate of two species' making it 'difficult to link' treatments to effects, concluding 'validation experiment needs to be re-conducted.'

Agreement on CK manipulation failure (C32-C33, C97-C99). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the problematic failure to reduce C. kiiensis eDNA undermines conclusions. Peer reviewers similarly criticize inadequate validation of species fate after introduction.

Disagreement on gene expression results (C41-C45). OpenEval finds RNA-seq results supported despite location effects and transient changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing inability to 'link between rice gene expression after treatments and effectiveness of two species' due to inadequate tracking of introduced organisms.

Disagreement on DEG findings (C46-C48, C53). OpenEval supports the statistical findings while noting lack of validation. Peer reviewers question the fundamental linkage between treatments and gene expression, stating it's 'difficult to link' without tracking species fate.

Agreement on speculative mechanisms (C49-C52, C54-C55, C100). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to substantial speculation without direct evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly question these mechanisms by emphasizing lack of validation and need to understand 'fitness and robustness' and track 'fate of two species.'

Partial overlap on growth effects interpretation (C49-C50). OpenEval questions CK effects given failed manipulation. Peer reviewers note modest effects and incomplete validation, criticizing lack of tracking 'fate of two species after introducing into rice.'

Agreement on G. nunn selection (C22-C23, C88). OpenEval supports the rationale as reasonable for proof-of-concept. Peer reviewers accept species selection despite noting 'no strong rationale,' acknowledging 'method has enough novelty' for proof-of-concept purposes.

Agreement on C. kiiensis selection (C24-C25, C89-C90). OpenEval supports the rationale with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers similarly accept the selection for proof-of-concept despite lack of strong rationale, acknowledging methodological novelty.

Partial overlap on experimental design (C26-C28, C91, C95). OpenEval supports the design while noting cross-contamination concerns. Peer reviewers focus more on validation issues, criticizing that authors didn't adequately track species fate after introduction.

Partial overlap on UIC analysis (C15, C19-C20). OpenEval supports the analysis while noting multiple testing concerns. Peer reviewers acknowledge the framework but express concern that 'current results did not fully support' the approach's effectiveness.

Minimal overlap on eDNA metabarcoding data (C14). OpenEval fully supports the methodology and temporal patterns. Peer reviewers acknowledge the approach but focus on whether it effectively identifies influencing organisms, rating overall conclusions as UNCERTAIN.

Minimal overlap on knowledge gaps (C21). OpenEval supports honest assessment of limitations. Peer reviewers emphasize study is 'too preliminary' and needs 'more data and evidence,' suggesting more fundamental concerns about the approach.
Minimal overlap on experimental summary (C76). OpenEval supports the accurate summary. Peer reviewers accept species selection as reasonable for proof-of-concept without challenging the summary.

Minimal overlap on G. nunn emphasis (C78). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment that GN showed clearer effects than CK. Peer reviewers note modest effects and incomplete validation but don't specifically challenge the differential emphasis.

OpenEval evaluates 2017 observational study setup and monitoring protocol (C10-C13, C75, C81-C83) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details of the initial observational phase.

OpenEval rates application of Takens' embedding theorem (C59, C74) as UNCERTAIN, questioning its applicability to noisy biological systems. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this theoretical justification.

OpenEval supports acknowledgment of taxonomic identification limitations (C107-C108), noting only 52 of 718 ASVs had species-level identification. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this limitation.

OpenEval supports methodological details and quality controls for larval removal (C119-C127), though notes disconnect between larvae removed and eDNA persistence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological details.
OpenEval supports background and motivation claims (C1-C5, C63-C65) as well-cited and appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory framing claims.

OpenEval supports eDNA metabarcoding background (C6-C8, C70-C71) as accurately describing capabilities with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological background.
OpenEval supports nonlinear time series methods background (C9, C72-C73) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this analytical background.
OpenEval supports description of classical ecological approaches and limitations (C66-C69) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this motivational framing.
